newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fresh violence erupts in Indonesian town.
newsitem.headline: Fresh violence erupts in Indonesian town.

text.p: Indonesian troops were called out in the central Java town of Pekalongan on Tuesday when supporters of rival political parties clashed, residents said.
"Armed soldiers are stationed in the town. Many shops are closed today because the owners are afraid of fresh violence," said a resident.
Police in Pekalongan, 300 km (190 miles) east of Jakarta, declined to comment.

Residents said hundreds of people who apparently were supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) attacked a housing estate mostly inhabited by civil servants late on Monday night.
Civil servants are usually supporters of the ruling Golkar party.
"A number of motorcycles were burned, but there were no reports of injuries or arrests," said one resident.

Pekalongan, a stronghold of the PPP, was rocked by violence two weeks ago. The party's flags were removed by cadres of Golkar before a popular singer, who used to campaign for PPP but is now a Golkar candidate for the May 29 general elections, was due to visit the area.
Sporadic clashes have recurred since then and residents say the situation is tense.

Meanwhile, in Rengasdengklok, West Java, an Indonesian man of Chinese descent was jailed for inciting a riot in January during which churches and Chinese temples were attacked, Kompas newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The newspaper said Tjio Kim Tjoan, 55, was sentenced on Monday to three years and six months in jail after being found guilty of provoking the riot in Rengasdengklok, 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta.
It quoted judges as saying Tjio had scolded Moslem youths who were beating drums to summon people to eat before the start of daytime fasting during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
A mainly Moslem mob later attacked churches and Chinese temples and looted homes and shops. Sixteen cars were also burned.
